newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania takes in 64 pct of 1997 wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Romania takes in 64 pct of 1997 wheat harvest.

text.p: Romania has taken in 64 percent of its 1997 wheat crop and figures show a good average yield, but recent rains have delayed harvesting and damaged over 180,000 hectares put under wheat, an official said on Tuesday.
"So far, we harvested 4.749 million tonnes of wheat from 1.53 million hectares," an agriculture ministry official said.
Average yield per hectare was 3,103 kg, compared to the ministry's initial estimates of 2,963, the official said.
Official estimates put Romania's 1997 wheat crop at around seven million tonnes and exports at over two million.
Some experts say that heavy rains and floods in recent weeks might substantially reduce this figure.

Latest ministry data showed flood and rains had damaged 185,600 ha under wheat and that harvesting was behind schedule. The high humidity in the soil had prevented farmers from using harvesting equipment in the fields, the official said.
"This figure might be bigger as it doesn't include the effects of the adverse weather over the past four days," he said in reference to heavy rains which have hit Romania since the weekend.
On Monday, the independent daily Adevarul said the rains had a "devastating" impact on the wheat crop in some areas of the southern Romanian Plain, Romania's main grain suppliers.
Data recorded in over 20 localities in the Romanian Plain showed rain levels amounted to 150 litres per square metre on Saturday.
"Some 250,000 unharvested ha are in danger," Adevarul said. Experts had put daily losses at 150 kg per ha, it said.
"The ministry has no new estimates for the 1997 wheat crop," the official said.
